chunks: The evil eye is real, and charm (ruqya) is real, and sorcery is real, and fa'l (auguring good) is real, while tiyarah (auguring evil) is not real, and spreading of a disease from one to the other is not real. Scent gives pleasure, honey gives pleasure, riding gives pleasure, and looking at greenery gives pleasure.

key_terms.الطِّيَرَةُ: Bad augury or taking omen of evil
key_terms.الْعَيْنُ: The evil eye (effect of a gaze)
key_terms.الْفَأْلُ: Good augury or taking omen of good

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between fa'l and tiyarah in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) delineates the boundary between authentic metaphysical realities—such as the evil eye, sorcery, and contagious disease—and mere superstitions like bad omens, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual causality with rational observation. By categorizing sensory pleasures like honey and greenery as 'nushrah' (a share or portion of delight), he validates worldly enjoyment as a divine blessing rather than a distraction, a concept deeply rooted in the Quranic affirmation of lawful pleasures.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 400. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

Evil effect of sight is right; charm is right; sorcery is right, and fa’l (auguring good) is right, while ṭiyarah (auguring evil) [1] is not right, and spreading of a disease from one to the other is not right. Scent gives pleasure, honey gives pleasure, riding gives pleasure and looking at greenery gives pleasure.
